chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Basir, and 'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, both of them, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the one 'who holds the knot of marriage,' so he said: 'He is the father, the brother, the one to whom the will is entrusted, and the one whose authority is valid over the woman's property from among her relatives, who sells for her and buys.' He said: 'So whichever of these forgives, his forgiveness is valid regarding the dowry when he forgives it.'

key_terms.الْمَهْر: Dowry; the gift given by the husband to the wife
key_terms.الْمَوْصِي إِلَيْهِ: The one to whom the will is entrusted; executor
key_terms.عَفْوٌ: Forgiveness; remission of a right or debt
key_terms.عُقْدَةُ النِّكَاحِ: The knot of marriage; the legal bond or authority in the marriage contract

ai.seo_question: Who has the authority to forgive the dowry in a Shia marriage contract?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi's *Tahdhib* clarifies the concept of 'the one in whose hand is the knot of marriage' by identifying the wali (guardian) as the father, brother, or a relative authorized to manage the woman's estate. It establishes that the forgiveness of the mahr (dowry) by any of these authorized guardians is legally binding, reflecting the Shia juristic view on the validity of the wali's consent and financial authority in marital contracts.
